In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SUSY accompanied light neutrino exchange mechanism is the most promising one to explain 0νβ decay, but its contribution to 0\nuββ decay half-lives is still below the current experimental limits.
the SUSY accompanied light Majorana neutrinos exchange mechanism is unlikely to be responsible for the 0νβ decay of heavy nuclei.
the SUSY accompanied Majorana neutrino mechanism of 0νβ decay, if it exists, is not yet ruled out by the current experimental limits.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SUSY contributions to 0ν ββ decay half-life are suppressed, and are unlikely to be enhanced by a factor of 10 6 as claimed by Babu and M.
the SUSY contribution to the light neutrino exchange mechanism is negligible compared to the light neutrinos contribution.
the SUSY contributions are not significant for the light neutrino mass range allowed by current experimental data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SUSY accompanied mechanism of 0νβbb decay, if it exists at all, is suppressed relative to the standard light Majorana neutrinos exchange mechanism by at least four orders of magnitude.
, while the SUSY contributions are not very significant, they are nonnegligible and should be included in any analysis of 0νβ ββ decay.
